title: Toyota Mega Cruiser
verdict: Toyota's answer to the Humvee: 2.17 metres wide, portal hubs, four-wheel steering and three locking diffs, driven by a 4.1-litre four-cylinder diesel from a truck. Only 133 were registered as civilian cars in Japan, so the hardest part of owning one is finding one.

paragraphs: The Mega Cruiser is the largest 4WD Toyota has ever built, and it exists because the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force wanted its own Humvee. The military version is the Kōkidōsha, or High Mobility Vehicle, model code BXD10. In January 1996 Toyota put a civilian version on sale in Japan, the BXD20V, aimed at disaster rescue rather than the school run. It shares nothing with any [[land-cruiser/80-series|80 Series]] or [[land-cruiser/70-series|70 Series]] except the badge and the attitude, and it looks enough like an [[hummer/h1|H1]] that Japan nicknamed it the 'Japanese Hummer'.

story.heading: THE KŌKIDŌSHA
paragraphs: Toyota developed and supplied the High Mobility Vehicle, which Japanese sources say Hino builds. From 1993 the JGSDF put test batches with its trials unit, the Infantry School Regiment and the 1st Airborne Brigade, then trial-deployed it to 2nd Division units in 1994. Regular deliveries began with the 1st Infantry Regiment in spring 1995. It carries a ten-soldier squad, tows mortars and trailers, and became the base for missile launchers and other specialist versions. Troops call it the 'Kōki'.

The early trucks used the 15B-FT, a 4.1-litre direct-injection turbo-diesel four from Toyota's Dyna light trucks. Vehicles procured from fiscal 1999 to 2003 got the electronically injected 15B-FTE. From fiscal 2004 the HMV switched to Hino's N04C engine, which changed the model code to XCD10. Only the 15B-engined trucks are BXD10s. By the count in Japanese Wikipedia, more than 3,000 HMVs and derivatives have been built, and the JGSDF is still buying them.

story.heading: A RESCUE TRUCK FOR CIVILIANS
paragraphs: A prototype appeared at the 30th Tokyo Motor Show in October 1993. Toyota's launch release on 9 January 1996 pitched the Mega Cruiser at rescue and reconstruction work after natural disasters, and at research and exploration in harsh conditions. Final assembly was at Gifu Auto Body in Kakamigahara. It cost ¥9.62 million (¥9.8 million after the 1999 engine change), about the same as a Toyota Century or Honda NSX of the day, and there was no tachometer.

The buyers were mostly institutions: the Japan Automobile Federation (JAF), fire and rescue services and local governments. Gifu Prefectural Police run one as a disaster vehicle, the only Mega Cruiser police car in Japan. The Maritime Self-Defense Force chose the civilian Mega Cruiser rather than the HMV, and the Air Self-Defense Force uses it as an off-base rescue vehicle. Production ended in August 2001 and sales that December. According to Japanese sources, new registrations totalled 133, including some high-roof trucks that never appeared in the catalogue.

story.heading: HOW IT WORKS
paragraphs: Hub-reduction gears at each wheel let Toyota mount the drive shafts high and run 37-inch tires. Toyota quotes a practical ground clearance of 420 mm. To keep the space under the frame clear, the transmission, transfer case, prop shafts and differentials are all mounted as high as possible, which leaves a huge tunnel between the front seats. The brakes are inboard ventilated discs next to the differentials, because there's no room for them inside the hubs. Suspension is double wishbones on longitudinal torsion bars at all four corners.

Drive is full-time 4WD through a four-speed lockup automatic and a two-speed transfer case with a centre diff lock. Front and rear axles have Torsen limited-slip diffs, and each can be locked. Reverse-phase four-wheel steering turns the rear wheels up to 12 degrees, which gives a 5.6-metre turning radius on a 3,395 mm wheelbase. An optional system could deflate the rear tires on the move for mud and snow. One Japanese line sums it up: if you get this stuck, the only thing left is something with tracks.

story.heading: COMING OF AGE ABROAD
paragraphs: Mega Cruisers leaked out of Japan as gray imports to places like Australia and Russia. The first ones turned 25 in 2020–21, which made them legal to import into the US under NHTSA's 25-year rule. Jalopnik reported that the Land Cruiser Heritage Museum in Utah already had one. Since then Bring a Trailer has listed both civilian trucks and ex-military BXD10s. In 2026 Japan donated 30 HMVs to Ukraine.

In Japan the civilian truck has become hard to keep on the road. Ibaraki Prefecture sold the Mega Cruiser a local bank had donated to it for disaster duty, citing difficulty getting parts, and the 3,780 kg gross vehicle weight means a holder of a standard licence issued after March 2017 can't legally drive one there. Rare, enormous and short of spares, it's a truck for collectors with a plan.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · BXD10 VS BXD20
callout.title: Military, civilian and the in-between
paragraphs: BXD10 is the JGSDF's 15B-engined High Mobility Vehicle: a canvas or soft-top troop carrier with inward-facing rear benches, folding windscreen, run-flat inserts in its tires and a pintle hitch. BXD20V is the civilian five-door wagon with a hard roof, six seats, air conditioning, a side-hinged tailgate with a fold-out step and a spare tire lifted by a chain hoist.

Bring a Trailer listings show both. In 2024 an ex-military BXD10, repainted in Dubai and titled in Maryland as a 1990, was bid to $43,999 without selling. Civilian trucks have sold for $84,000 and $167,500. Most are right-hand drive. One BaT seller claimed only seven left-hand-drive examples were built, and Carscoops put the 2020 count at around twelve.

engineering_intro: The Mega Cruiser rides on a straight ladder frame with four-wheel independent suspension (double wishbones and longitudinal torsion bars) and hub-reduction gearing at each wheel. That gearing raises the half-shafts for 420 mm of clearance under 37-inch tires and adds a final reduction, so the truck can creep up steep grades on torque-converter creep alone. Full-time 4WD, a locking centre diff, Torsen front and rear diffs with their own locks, and hydraulic reverse-phase rear steer complete the package.

engineering.note: The HMV chassis was also used for longer-wheelbase Super Dyna and Coaster 4WD variants.
Direct injection, intercooled. 155 PS at 3,200 rpm and 39.0 kgm (282 lb-ft) at 1,800 rpm. Became the 15B-FTE (170 PS, 43.0 kgm) from May 1999.
Full-time 4WD with a centre diff lock. Torsen LSDs front and rear, each with a lock.
Double wishbones at all four corners. The long torsion bars and the weight give a good ride.
Brakes sit next to the diffs to cut unsprung weight. Backlash in the reduction gears makes the truck pitch under hard braking.
5.6 m turning radius. The rear steer centres itself on a spring when the hydraulics are off.

generations_table.note: Military Kōkidōsha. Trials from 1993, regular deliveries from spring 1995.
Electronic injection to meet stricter emissions rules.
Not a BXD10. Hino engine, still in production.

buying_checks.head: Civilian or military?
buying_checks.body: A BXD20V civilian wagon and an ex-JGSDF BXD10 soft-top are different trucks with different values. Ex-military trucks have arrived via third countries (one BaT truck was repainted in Dubai and titled as a 1990), so check the import paperwork and the chassis plate.

buying_checks.head: Do the 4WS and tire deflation work?
buying_checks.body: Several BaT trucks were sold with inoperative four-wheel steering or central tire inflation, or with parts such as the deflator hose missing. Check them, because these systems are part of what you're paying for.

buying_checks.head: Underbody rust
buying_checks.body: BaT sellers have noted rust on the underside, painted-over underbodies and rust repair before a repaint. Get under it with a light and a probe, especially around the hub-reduction housings and frame.

buying_checks.head: 24-volt electrics
buying_checks.body: The truck runs a 24-volt electrical system. Budget for batteries in pairs, and make sure any added accessories are wired for 24 V.

buying_checks.head: Parts supply
buying_checks.body: Ibaraki Prefecture sold its Mega Cruiser partly because parts were hard to get. The 15B engine family was also used in Dyna light trucks, which helps with engine service items, but body and driveline parts are specialist. Find your source before you buy.

buying_checks.head: Size and access
buying_checks.body: It's 2,170 mm wide, 5,090 mm long and 2,075 mm tall, so measure your garage, check parking and trail widths, and remember the high sills that need the grab handles.

buying_checks.head: Service records and import papers
buying_checks.body: Recent BaT trucks with records listed axle-shaft, wheel-bearing, motor-mount, gasket and differential-fluid work. Receipts like these, plus clean import documents and a title, add real value.

repairs.title: Hub-reduction and differential gear oil
repairs.symptoms: No records, weeping seals at the hub housings or diffs, or noise from the driveline.
repairs.fix: Drain and refill both differentials, the transfer case and all four hub-reduction housings with the oils specified in the factory manual. One BaT seller had the differentials serviced with fresh fluid before sale. Look for metal on the drain plugs and leaking seals while you're there.
repairs.tools: Factory manual for fill levels [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · drain pans · fluid pump

repairs.title: Rear axle shaft and wheel bearings
repairs.symptoms: Clunks, play or noise at a corner. BaT trucks have had a left-rear axle shaft replaced and the wheel bearings serviced.
repairs.fix: Support the truck safely (it weighs about 2.9 tonnes), remove the wheel and hub-reduction assembly following the factory manual, and replace the worn shaft or bearings. Refill the hub housing with fresh oil.
repairs.tools: Heavy-duty jack and stands rated for 3+ tonnes · factory manual · bearing tools

repairs.title: Engine and transmission mounts
repairs.symptoms: Vibration or clunking on take-off. One BaT truck had both its motor mounts and front mounts replaced.
repairs.fix: Support the engine, unbolt and replace the mounts, then check the exhaust and driveshaft clearances.

repairs.title: Engine gaskets and leaks (15B-FT)
repairs.symptoms: Oil seeping from the sump, valve cover or exhaust manifold. One BaT truck had the oil pan, valve cover and exhaust manifold gaskets replaced, plus a coolant reservoir hose.
repairs.fix: Clean the engine, find each leak and replace the gaskets. Because the 15B is a light-truck diesel, a Toyota truck dealer may be able to source engine gaskets more easily than body parts.
repairs.tools: Metric sockets · gasket scraper · torque wrench

repairs.title: Fuel filter and batteries
repairs.symptoms: Hard starting, or a truck that has been sitting. BaT trucks had fuel filters and batteries replaced after import.
repairs.fix: Replace the fuel filter and bleed the system. Fit matched batteries for the 24 V system and check the charging voltage.
repairs.tools: Basic hand tools · fuel filter wrench · multimeter

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: It already wears 37s. Japanese sources give the factory tire as 37x12.50R17.5 LT, and BaT trucks run 37x12.50 tires on 17-inch steel or aftermarket wheels. We found no owner reports of going bigger. With hub reduction and 420 mm of clearance, it doesn't need more.

No. It shares the Cruiser name and Toyota's off-road ethos, but it's a separate design built from the JGSDF High Mobility Vehicle, with hub reduction, independent suspension at all four corners and four-wheel steering.

Japanese sources put civilian new-car registrations at 133. The Drive cites the same figure from Toyota. The military HMV is a different story: more than 3,000 have been built including derivatives, and it's still in production with Hino engines.

faq.q: Can I import one to the US?
faq.a: Yes. The first trucks became eligible under NHTSA's 25-year rule from 2020–21, and several are now titled in the US. Check your state's emissions and titling rules, and get the import paperwork with the truck.

The 15B-FT, a 4,104 cc direct-injection turbo-diesel four with an intercooler: 155 PS at 3,200 rpm and 39.0 kgm (282 lb-ft) at 1,800 rpm. From May 1999 it became the electronically injected 15B-FTE, with 170 PS and 43.0 kgm.
Three. The centre diff locks through the two-speed transfer case, and the front and rear Torsen limited-slip diffs each have a lock as standard.
Reverse-phase rear steering turns the rear wheels up to 12 degrees, for a 5.6-metre turning radius despite a 3,395 mm wheelbase.

faq.q: What tire pressures does it run?
faq.a: Japanese sources give unequal pressures: 140 kPa front and 240 kPa rear, chosen for rough-terrain performance. The optional system could lower the rear pressures on the move.

On Bring a Trailer, civilian trucks have sold for $167,500 (January 2024) and $84,000 (June 2025), and other civilian trucks were bid to $82,000–144,000 without selling. Ex-military BXD10s were bid to $32,025–43,999 in 2024 without selling.

faq.q: What fuel economy and range does it get?
faq.a: The Drive reports that Toyota quoted about 22 mpg at a constant 37 mph, with a 28.5-gallon tank. Real-world highway economy isn't documented.

baseline_service.intro: No factory owner's manual or service data for the Mega Cruiser is available online in English, so this list gives the systems to baseline and leaves the fluid specs for you to confirm in the Japanese factory manual. Assume nothing has been done since import unless there are receipts.
